correctness.rationale: Translate into the difference span H. Rank three gives the affine simplex. In rank two put three points at 0,e1,e2; avoiding the three lines leaves (1,1),(1,2),(2,1), each giving a parallelogram after reordering. Equal character restrictions to H give proportional columns. Thus an invertible minor requires four different restrictions and each unordered local set has exactly (3^(d-r))^4 lifts, with unchanged Gram spectrum. Frequency translation is row-phase multiplication, and the count of (set, distinguished member) pairs is both four times the unanchored count and 3^r times the zero-anchored count. The independent exact calculation (column Gram traces plus Newton identities, not the packaged principal-minor implementation) reproduced the five planar polynomial multiplicities 16,4,16,16,4 in the order given. The first factors into t^2-9t+9 and t^2-7t+9, giving the stated extremes; the second has ratio 9, the third has cubic roots in (0,1),(4,5),(7,8) and so ratio >7; the remaining two are singular. In rank three all off-diagonal squared moduli are at least one by the integer root multiplicities, so tr(Q^2)>=76, tr(Q)=16. If the eigenvalue ratio is at most 7/3, scale into [1,7/3]; the derivative of (x^2+S)/(x+T)^2 is proportional to xT-S, so each coordinate maximum is at an endpoint and no interior coordinate attains the global maximum. The endpoint cases with 0 through 4 high values give 1/4,19/64,29/100,13/48,1/4. Only a single high value reaches 76/256, forcing spectrum (7,3,3,3) at equality and ruling out any smaller ratio. Of 2600 anchored simplex sets exactly eight have second characteristic coefficient 90 (tr(Q^2)=76), all with polynomial (t-7)(t-3)^3. The unanchored counts are therefore 16*9/4=36 and 8*27/4=54 before lifts. value.rationale: The exact optimal Riesz ratio is intrinsic to a sampling support and measures whether its best exponential basis is numerically stable; the multiplicity tells how many distinct bases attain that stability. The two affine geometries are exhaustive at this size and their sharp ratios differ substantially. This is a motivated finite classification, with an analytic quantitative lower bound and exact arithmetic in precisely justified representative spaces, not just an arbitrary table or reproduced rank counts.
